title: A fixed dimensionless parameter need not determine a unique scaling limit
problem: Determine whether the regular octagon's approximate-to-exact collision ratio has a unique limit when n*r^2=1.
failure: R11 proposed n*r^2 as a candidate crossover variable, not a theorem. R12 disproves sufficiency in the sharp disk model: two adjacent-integer subsequences have distinct limits even with the variable fixed exactly.
correction: Use the Pell-unit automorphism of the even lattice to renormalize the observation disk; prove summable bounds for the local-limit terms; retain the boundary contribution. The exact difference of the two limits is 8/e.
transfer: Before accepting a one-parameter scaling collapse, inspect hidden arithmetic scale phases and construct subsequences approaching an observation boundary from both sides. Separate a proven jump from numerical estimates of each limiting value.
limits: Author-derived result for the regular unit octagon at r=1/sqrt(n) with a sharp closed-disk cutoff. Six exact finite-size counts, 2401 bounded unit checks; truncated Gaussian sums are numerical proxies without certified decimal error. No independent validation, novelty assessment, physical interpretation or general smoothing result.
